Chart how spend moves across a set of scenarios

Source: R/charts.R
ec_compare.Rd

A slope chart: one line per line item, one position per scenario. The picture of mediaplanr::compare_scenarios() at cell level — a cut is a line falling, an addition a line rising from zero, and a cell owned by a subplan is flat by construction, because no scenario can edit it.

Usage

ec_compare(x, by = NULL, theme = "light")

Arguments

x

A ScenarioSet, or the data frame mediaplanr::compare_scenarios() returns at level = "cell".

by

Columns identifying a line to draw. Defaults to the set's line item grain — the grain without its time column — so a weekly set draws one line per line item rather than one per cell-week. Required when x is a data frame with no obvious line item columns.

theme

A viz_theme() name or override list.

Value

A new_spec() of kind "compare".

See also

ec_lineage(), mediaplanr::compare_scenarios()

Examples

base <- mediaplanr::media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"), channel = c("TV", "Search"),
             planned_spend = c(80, 40)),
  grain = "channel", time = "week", name = "base"
)
s1  <- mediaplanr::build_scenario(
  base, list(target = list(channel = "Search"), total = 60), name = "Search up")
set <- mediaplanr::add_scenario(mediaplanr::scenario_set(base), s1)
ec_compare(set)
#> <mediaplanr_spec> compare
#>   from    compare_scenarios(set, "cell")
#>   series  2
#>   size    1,677 bytes of JSON
#>   meta    scenarios, cells, by
#> 
#>   as_widget() to draw it, as_json() to send it
